notes: Warm 180-frame samples, 1400x900 CSS pixels at device scale 1; headless Chrome, ANGLE Metal, Apple M4 Pro.
CPU submit times cover the main Three.js render, not asynchronous GPU completion or the brain inset.
Active simulation samples are live and nondeterministic; compare the actual limits, not a guaranteed FPS.
Earlier tuning runs were excluded after hot reload and transient frame-time interference; these samples used the separate HMR-disabled server on port 5174.
Final adaptive resolution run. Device scale is 1, but the render DPR drops to 0.9 in active macro and begins recovering in the subsequent wide sample; per-scenario DPR is recorded.

Retina final check: device scale 2, 5-second adaptation warmup, then 120 frames per page, paused macro views. Effective render DPR settled near 0.997 with full geometry retained. Front/rear/top/eye-close screenshots also inspected.

The before/after table and initial Retina check precede the material revision. materialRevision records the reduced sheen, filtered surface texture, amber light wrap and restrained wing/eye reflections; same hardware, browser, viewport and 180-frame harness. Live worker timings vary between runs.

Blender detail revision: a shared 512-square packed data tile replaces procedural cuticle noise; facial hairs are shorter and denser. Reported active-simulation FPS remains workload dependent; the short social sample is supplemented by a separate 600-frame check after ten seconds of simulation warmup.

Current fly.html is always interactive 3D. blenderInteractive records the Blender-subdivided geometry, Cycles body/hair irradiance and AgX display transform. The earlier renderedPage gallery was removed; its measurements are historical only.

notes: Production fly page: 1400x900 CSS pixels, Chrome 152/ANGLE Metal, M4 Pro, 300 warm frames per view, device scale 1.
The default, head and flight views retain 1,169,030 body triangles plus instanced hairs. The diffuse bake replaces screen-space AO.
The 9,261,127-byte mesh includes the original sampler, subdivided geometry and body/hair lighting. No fly photographs load.
Retina sample: 8 seconds warmup then 180 frames, actual render density reported separately from device scale.
Baked diffuse lighting follows the fixed studio/rest pose. Gloss, wings and camera interaction are live; pose-dependent self-shadowing and female scattering remain approximations.
Arena regression checks use its dynamic-lighting appearance and verify all five workers advance; these are render FPS measurements, not neural throughput.
Separate production builds, Chrome 152 on Apple M4 Pro, ANGLE Metal, 1400x900, DPR 1 fixed during profiling, 240 frames per view after 1.8 seconds warmup.
GPU timers run separately from ordinary frame profiling because ANGLE instrumentation can serialize GPU work.
Loading uses three fresh browser contexts with the HTTP cache disabled on a local server; OS and driver caches remain warm. CPU-throttled loading is one 4x run, not a phone measurement.

afterFrames predates the final material-clone startup fix, which does not change the render loop. afterLoading and validation use that fix. CPU submission times varied between runs; no percentage improvement is claimed.
No geometry, hairs, MSAA samples or shadow resolution removed. The body-only half-resolution focus depth pass is replaced with the full-resolution resolved color depth, including opaque hairs.
WebGPU adapter/device initialization succeeded on apple metal-3, with timestamp-query support. The fly graphics renderer is still WebGL 2; no WebGPU speedup is claimed.

notes: Uncapped Chrome with --disable-frame-rate-limit --disable-gpu-vsync; 600 frames per view after 5 seconds warmup, device DPR 2, adaptive raster resolution. These are throughput averages, not proof of 120 Hz physical presentation or a guarantee that every frame is below 8.33 ms.

The initial strict both-page run failed the dark flying view at 79.3 FPS. Isolating wing ghosts identified expensive overlapping per-fragment area-light shading. The final run uses smooth per-vertex illumination for the same 16 wing-stroke samples; resting wing materials are unchanged.

Both pages now target 120 Hz when refresh sampling detects a fast display. 60 Hz displays retain their original resolution policy. A successful high-refresh raster size is held until resize to avoid recurring MSAA allocations.

Fly shadows keep the same geometry, 1024-square map and 30 Hz upper limit; updates are skipped when all caster bounds move less than half a shadow texel. Camera damping and double-click focus are time-based.
Final throughput builds precede only the sustained refresh-transition guard; that guard is independently covered by check_render_resolution.mjs and the final browser interaction check.
